content_text_body:
The goal is to learn how to plan out projects so that you know what resources are needed to successfully complete them.

 Prior to the next project start, estimate the time, materials, people and technical resources it will take to complete it. Add buffer time for issues that may arise.

 Ensure your plans will provide all the tools the team needs, including software, hardware or any other outside resources.

 Make sure you have enough people hours. If not, plan to accomplish whatever is feasible with the number of people you have at the time (i.e., reduce the scope but keep the deadline). Or, extend the deadline to fit the capacity of available people hours. If your own time seems to be overcommitted, track it for a couple of weeks to see where you're spending too much time.

 Get regular updates from your team to better understand how long each task takes, and if there are any additional tools, supplies or information they need, etc.

 Determine when you should invest in new resources. If there is a reason why you cannot purchase new tools and add additional team members, be transparent about it with your team.

 Ensure your tools are adequate for the tasks at hand. Do you have enough? Are they outdated? Are they working properly? Is there a more efficient tool available.
